name: Purpose Pilot llms.txt Connector
author: luisathautelocals

sections.description:
Purpose Pilot llms.txt Connector is made by The Purpose Pilot, the healthcare marketing brand (DBA) of Haute Locals, for the websites of practices it manages.

llms.txt is a plain-text file at the root of a website that tells AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and others) which pages matter most and what they cover.

Most llms.txt plugins build the file automatically from your posts and pages. This plugin does not generate anything. The Purpose Pilot’s team researches, writes and reviews each client’s llms.txt in its own marketing platform, keeps it current as the site and services change, and publishes it to the site through the standard WordPress REST API using an administrator application password the site owner authorizes. The plugin is the small receiving end of that workflow.

What the plugin does:

  • Adds a /llms.txt address to your site that returns the stored text as plain text.
  • Registers one setting (purpose_pilot_llms_txt) that administrators can read and update through the WordPress REST API.
  • Registers a setting (purpose_pilot_schema_jsonld) for the homepage business schema (JSON-LD: practice name, address, phone). Only valid schema.org JSON is accepted, and it is printed on the homepage only. Empty means nothing is added.
  • If Yoast SEO or Rank Math is active, lets users who can edit a page update that page’s SEO title, meta description and social (Open Graph and X) title and description through the REST API. Neither plugin allows this on its own, so approved title changes made outside wp-admin were dropped. After a change, the page’s cache is cleared when WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache or SiteGround Optimizer is active, so the change shows right away.
  • Optional, off by default: registers a setting (purpose_pilot_lead_tracker_id). When an administrator stores the site’s client id there, the site loads The Purpose Pilot’s lead attribution script on public pages (see External services).

What it does not do:

  • The plugin itself makes no outgoing requests from your server.
  • Unless an administrator stores schema or turns on lead attribution, it adds nothing to your pages, theme or admin screens.
  • It does not create files on your server.
  • It does not change any page content.

If the stored text is empty, /llms.txt returns a 404, as if the plugin were not installed.

External services

Lead attribution (only when an administrator turns it on by storing a client id in purpose_pilot_lead_tracker_id):

  • What: visitors’ browsers load a script from The Purpose Pilot’s platform at https://altitude.thepurposepilot.com/leads-tracker.js.
  • Why: to count form submissions and phone or email link clicks on the site and record which marketing source (search, ad, campaign link, referrer) brought the visitor, so the practice can see which marketing produces leads.
  • Data sent: the page address, referrer, campaign (UTM) parameters, and the fact that a form was submitted or a phone or email link was clicked, with the site’s client id. If the site uses Google Analytics, the same events are also sent to the site’s own Google Analytics, without personal information.
  • Terms of service: https://altitude.thepurposepilot.com/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://altitude.thepurposepilot.com/privacy

Clearing the setting (or deactivating the plugin) stops the script from loading.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (Plugins, Add New, search for “Purpose Pilot llms.txt Connector”), or let The Purpose Pilot install it through your site’s WordPress connection.
  2. The Purpose Pilot publishes your llms.txt from its platform.
  3. Visit yoursite.com/llms.txt to confirm the text is live.
sections.faq:
Do I need to be a client of The Purpose Pilot?

The plugin only serves text that an administrator stores through the REST API. It is built for sites managed by The Purpose Pilot. If you want an llms.txt generated from your own content, a generator plugin is a better fit.

Another plugin (for example an SEO plugin) also creates llms.txt.

Only one can answer at /llms.txt. A physical llms.txt file in your site root takes priority over this plugin. Turn off the other plugin’s llms.txt feature to use this one.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating removes the /llms.txt address. Deleting the plugin also deletes the stored text, the schema and the lead attribution setting. SEO titles and descriptions already saved stay with your SEO plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Homepage business schema (JSON-LD), stored through the REST API.
  • Yoast SEO and Rank Math title, description and social fields can be updated through the REST API by users who can edit the page.
  • Clears the page cache of common cache plugins after one of these changes.

1.1.0

  • Optional lead attribution script, off by default, turned on by an administrator through the REST API.

1.0.0

  • First release: serves /llms.txt from a setting managed through the REST API.
